s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of mild headaches with a mass in the parietal bone
salient_findings: Mild headaches of several months’ duration
19-mm mass in the left parietal bone
Lesion isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images with internal hyperintense foci
key_facts: Mild headaches of several months’ duration
Previous cranial MRI 4 years earlier showed no significant change in the lesion
Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a well-defined mass in the left parietal bone
Lesion centered in the diploic space with sparse but preserved trabeculae
Slight bony bulge without disruption of the inner or outer tables
Lesion isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images
Lesion with multiple internal hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images

shortlist.label: Hemangioma of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined mass in the diploic space with preserved trabeculae and isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined mass in the parietal bone with slight bony bulge

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion centered in the diploic space with sparse but preserved trabeculae and heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion with multiple internal hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images and restricted diffusion on MRI

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion with heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images and expanded bone contour

raw.rationale: The lesion's appearance on MRI, being isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images with multiple internal hyperintense foci representing bone marrow fat, and its location in the diploic space with preserved trabeculae, is consistent with a hemangioma of bone.

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteomas are typically well-defined, benign bone tumors that are usually smaller and more densely calcified than the described lesion.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia often presents with a more ground-glass appearance on radiographs and may have a more significant impact on the surrounding bone structure.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
rejected.why: Eosinophilic granuloma typically presents with a more aggressive appearance, including destruction of the inner and outer tables of the skull, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are usually more expansile and may have a fluid-fluid level on MRI, which is not described in this case.
